title: Classify saturated headers by the sphere-braid relation and Hurwitz orbits (no κ)
body:
**No new κ.** A saturated header is a product of `n+1` square-zero rank-one units on `n` fields equal to `-I`. The package proves that it is the matrix image of the sphere-braid relation on a chain of transvections, that Hurwitz moves act on it linearly through the Burau representation at `t = -1`, and that in a fixed integral frame its Hurwitz orbits are classified exactly by the mod-2 multiset of the unit vectors (`|Sp_n(F_2)|/(n+1)!` orbits: 1, 6, 288 enumerated for `n = 2, 4, 6`). It also proves an arc law for site masks and reproduces literal Hurwitz words between the chain-nested roots and the root of #6726.

Results, each with its hypotheses (`char != 2`, `n` even, exactly `n+1` units; for path form `q^2 = 1`, `E(q) = 0`, ordinary controls absorbed, `D = 1`):
- **Rigidity.** Any two normalised headers on `F^n` differ by exactly one `g in GL_n(F)`; Hurwitz moves never create a new abstract root.
- **Sphere relation.** `tau_0...tau_{N-1}tau_{N-1}...tau_0 = -I + 2 rho e_0^*`, which is `-I` on `V/rad` exactly when `N` is odd (proved directly for all `N`; checked for `N <= 40`).
- **Path theorem.** A path-form header has tridiagonal Gram with every adjacent product `-1` (no other value); the chain realises it for every even `n`. Exhaustive on `F^2` with entries in `{-1,0,1}`: 160 solutions, all of this shape.
- **Hurwitz action.** A move is the linear action of the transvection along `x_i - x_{i+1}`; the images satisfy the braid relations; the orbit is the image of the braid group applied to the tuple. Only the two moved units change. Within the sector algebra `F[q]/(q^2-1)` a moved unit is again a sector unit; in path form the conjugate of adjacent units has a nonzero `q`-even part, so path-form moves are not available.
- **Classification.** In an integral frame, two headers are Hurwitz equivalent iff their `{x_t mod 2}` multisets agree. This uses one cited theorem (`rho(PB_{2g+1}) = Sp_{2g}(Z)[2]`, Brendle–Margalit Theorem 3.3), checked independently only at small level: orbit sizes mod 3, 4, 8 for `n = 2, 4` (12, 24, 96; 25920, 61440).
- **Arc law.** With `Omega = S_n` and 2-locally integral `x`, a mask containing the supports of `x` and `y` contains one of the two cyclic arcs between the two odd coordinates (all fields if their number is odd); `y` alone is not enough (counterexample included). Checked on 83,562 vectors and on literal roots and Hurwitz walks.
- **Literal words.** All 40 chains `(a|b)`, `n = 4..12`, share frame and invariants; shortest words `(2|2)-(3|2)` 2 letters, `(3|2)-(1|4)` 4, `(3|3)-(5|1)`, `(3|3)-(1|5)`, `(5|5)-(7|3)` 6. The root of #6726 is exactly 5 letters from chain `(3|3)` after a signed relabeling of its fields (one instance; no general statement about retirements).

Corrections found while reproving: the Birman–Hilden source gives the interpretation, not the relation (Fadell–Van Buskirk); the level-2 theorem is cited to Brendle–Margalit, with A'Campo credited there for the first statement (his paper was not available); the arc law needs both supports; the thin-query closed form of the chain family at shapes `(even|odd)` does not give a sign-Gram header (checked at `(2|1)`, `(2|3)`, `(4|1)`). Not covered: central `q` of order 3, non-central controls, non-uniform columns, characteristic 2, more than `n+1` units, non-integral frames, and any pricing.

Base: 7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a. The one pull-request input (the root of #6726 at 435bbe91fb28cb1d7a569ca70c6c4e9eb302d486) is an unmodified copy pinned in `retained/SOURCE-PINS.json`; the chain family follows #6833 at 51f54e3c31f2f3a3e056a483b3ed66ae916ad06a.

Reproduce (CPython 3.12, standard library):
```sh
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/p104-header-braid-classification
```
Expected: `PASS_HEADER_BRAID_CLASSIFICATION` (normal and `-O`) and `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`.

Overlap: searches of open and closed pull requests for Hurwitz, Burau, orbit, sphere-braid and braid-group terms found nothing on this object; related but different are #6817 (concave Coxeter batch tariffs), #2738, #6550 and #6655 (shortest words for a fixed endpoint) and #4900.
